linkedin_post:
Every time we talk to a new client about custom software, they think we are going to give them a bigger system to manage.

More dashboards. More fields to fill out. More steps.

It should be the exact opposite. 

Great software doesn't add steps to your day. It quietly removes the ones nobody wanted to do in the first place—like copying data between three different tools, chasing approvals over email, or building the same status report every single morning.

When you build around how your team actually works, the best feedback you can get is silence: nobody talking about the tool, because it just did the job.

Which manual step slows your team down the most?
